name: Verduno Pelaverga

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Dolcetto, Nebbiolo, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo and Merlot fully without cooking off their freshness.
Nebbiolo and Dolcetto sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.

sheet.place: Verduno Pelaverga is a light, spicy red from the little Pelaverga Piccolo grape. It comes from the village of Verduno in the Langhe, next to Barolo, and is made in tiny amounts.

claims.claim: Verduno Pelaverga (also Verduno) is a DOC with rules set by ministerial decree of 20 October 1995 (Gazzetta Ufficiale 270, 18 November 1995). Later amendments are reported in 2007, 2011, 2014 and 2015.
The wine must be 85% to 100% Pelaverga Piccolo. Up to 15% may be other non-aromatic red grapes from approved Piedmont vineyards.
There is one type: a still, dry red. Minimum alcohol is 11% by volume.
The zone is the whole commune of Verduno in the province of Cuneo, plus small parts of La Morra and Roddi.
Verduno is a small commune of 7.16 sq km at 381 m, bordering Bra, La Morra, Roddi and Santa Vittoria d'Alba. It is also one of the 11 communes of the Barolo zone.
Verduno's soils are mostly Sant'Agata marls, grey-blue and layered, with clay, limestone and sand in varying mixes, laid down in the Miocene.
The wine is ruby red, sometimes with violet tints. The nose is intense, fragrant, fruity and spicy. The palate is dry, fresh, velvety and balanced.

Pelaverga Piccolo has been grown in Verduno since the 15th century, though its origin is unclear. Tradition credits Blessed Sebastiano Valfre in the early 1700s, bringing it from Saluzzo. Castello di Verduno replanted with Pelaverga Piccolo in 1972, and others followed.
'Piccolo' refers to the small berries, which set it apart from the larger-berried Pelaverga grape of the Saluzzo area.
The name Pelaverga has competing explanations: a Latin 'pellis virga', or 'pela' and 'verga' (to peel a branch), tied to a way of training the vine.
The 2022 vintage registered 1,756 hl as DOC. Estimates of planted area range from about 11 to 21 hectares.
